canonicalExplanation.summary: Performance work starts with a **symptom learners feel**, such as slow typing, a janky scroll or a long first load, and then **evidence** of where the time goes. Check the React Profiler for slow renders, the browser Performance panel for long tasks, the Network panel for slow or big requests, and the bundle size for slow startup. Pick the fix that matches the cause: render fewer rows (pagination or virtualization), move state down so less re-renders, split code, or cache data. **Measure again** afterwards, and if nothing is actually slow, the right change is **no change**.

sections.heading: Start here
sections.body:
An admin page lists all 5,000 learner submissions. Typing in its filter box lags about half a second per key. Someone proposes wrapping every row in memo. Profiler evidence identifies a slow 5000-row render before pagination or virtualization is selected. In this lesson you'll record a render-performance observation and justify either a targeted optimization or no change.

```predict
{"question": "A component re-renders on every keystroke but each render takes 0.2 ms. Should you optimise it?", "options": ["Yes, every re-render is a bug", "No: it's fast enough; re-rendering is normal"], "answer": 1, "why": "Optimise measured slowness that users notice, not re-renders in general."}
```

sections.heading: Before you begin
sections.body: You should know the **Routing and application context** module, the **Remote data and asynchronous UI** module, **React developer tools** (the Profiler), and **Minimal and normalized state**, since smaller state can mean fewer re-renders.

sections.heading: The model: symptom, evidence, targeted fix, re-measure
sections.body:
| Symptom | Evidence to collect | Likely fix |
|---|---|---|
| typing lags. | Profiler: which component's render is slow. | render fewer items, move state down, memo a slow child. |
| long first load. | Network + bundle size. | code-split routes, smaller dependencies. |
| scroll janks. | Performance panel long tasks. | virtualize long lists, avoid layout thrash. |
| spinner for ages. | Network timings. | cache, paginate, fix the API. |

```text
Observation note.
Symptom: filter input lags ~500 ms per key.
Profiler: SubmissionList render 480 ms, 5000 SubmissionRow children.
Cause: every keystroke re-renders 5000 rows.
Fix chosen: paginate to 50 rows per page.
After: SubmissionList render 6 ms; typing feels instant.
```

```reveal
{"prompt": "Why paginate instead of memoizing each row?", "answer": "Memo still has to compare 5000 rows' props on every keystroke. Rendering 50 rows removes most of the work instead of skipping it one row at a time."}
```

sections.heading: When the answer is no change

includes: Record a symptom and profiler or network evidence before optimising.
Choose a targeted fix, or justify no change, and re-measure.
excludes: memo, useMemo and useCallback details (next lesson).

outcomes: Record a render-performance observation and justify either a targeted optimization or no change.

examples.title: The 5,000-row list
examples.situation: Profiler evidence identifies a slow 5000-row render before pagination or virtualization is selected.
walkthrough: **Symptom:** typing in the filter lags about half a second on each key.
**Profiler evidence:** SubmissionList takes 480 ms per commit, rendering all 5000 rows.
**Select and re-measure:** pagination to 50 rows will cut the render to about 6 ms; a second recording confirms it.
examples.result: Typing is instant again, and the change is justified by before-and-after measurements.

examples.title: The optimisation that did nothing
examples.situation: A developer wraps 30 small components in memo and useCallback "for speed". The app is no faster and the code is harder to read.
walkthrough: There was no measured slow render to begin with.
The real delay was a 2 MB chart library loaded on the home page.
Fix: remove the needless memo, lazy-load the chart route, and measure the first load.
examples.result: The home page loads faster, and the components are simple again.

misconceptions.mistakenBelief: Every rerender is a performance bug that should be prevented.
misconceptions.correction: Re-rendering is how React updates the screen and is usually cheap. Only renders that measurably slow down what learners do deserve optimisation, and the fix should match the measured cause.
misconceptions.diagnosticPrompt: In the opening predict, why wasn't the 0.2 ms render worth optimising?

analogy.example: Performance work is like **a doctor's visit**: start from the symptom ("it hurts when I type"), run the right test (Profiler, network), treat the actual cause, then check again. Handing out medicine for every organ (memo everywhere) doesn't cure anything.
limitations: Doctors can't undo treatments easily; you can revert code.
Some symptoms come from other departments: network or bundle, not React.

steps.explanation: Profiler evidence identifies a slow 5000-row render.

recap.summary: To record a render-performance observation, start from a symptom learners feel, gather Profiler, performance, network or bundle evidence, pick the fix that matches the cause such as pagination for a huge list, and re-measure, choosing no change when nothing is actually slow.
